title: Godot 4.6 breaking screen space fog shader for sky3D plugin
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.6 stable and 4.6.1 Rc1 - not reproducible in: 4.5.1 stable and earlier 4.xx versions ### System information Godot v4.6.1.rc1 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (NVIDIA; 27.21.14.6230) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory ### Issue description I started a new 4.6 fresh project and checked the world environment node without it the sky3d is looks fine, but with sky 3d having enabled the volumteric fog option it still looked completely normal, untill we add a camera and rotate it and see it in the camera perspective the weird artifact of half the screen getting a tint of some sorts, this goes away when volumetric fog is disable, fog option still works normally though. Below shows the artifact caused when the volumetric fog is enabled on sky3d on Godot 4.6: When screen space fog from SkyDome is enabled this issue occurs and when the volumetric fog is disabled from the env node under Sky3D this artifact tends to dissappear. Also if the screen space fog is not enabled at all, then even if volumetric fog and fog enabling on the world env under Sky3D node doesnt cause the artifacts. This issue never occured before 4.6 all earlier versions work absolutlely fine, but after 4.6 it seems to broken how this screen space fog shader works for Sky3d plugin. Below is how it looks with fog and volumetric fog enabled under Sky3D node and screen space fog enabled via SkyDome node in 4.5.1 Above shows no artifacts in camera view with all fogs enabled, seems like this screen space fog shader now breaks in 4.6 and 4.6.1 rc1. I have opened this issue under the sky3D repo as well: https://github.com/TokisanGames/Sky3D/issues/105 ### Steps to reproduce Steps to reproduce: 1. Under the MRP provided below can be opened in both 4.5.1 and 4.6.1 rc1 the node settings already saved to show the difference 2. First, enable fog and volumetric fog under [ Sky3D node -> environment -> fog (on) and volumetric fog (on) ] 3. Then enable fog ( screen space fog shader ) under the [ SkyDome node -> fog (on) ] 4. Now the artifact should appear through the camera perspective in 4.6. and 4.6.1 rc1. 5. This artifact now seemingly goes away by turning off [ Sky3D node -> environment -> volumetric fog (off) ] 6. Also goes away if screen space fog under SkyDome node -> fog (off) and keeping the volumetric fog [ Sky3D node -> environment -> fog (on/off) and volumetric fog (on /off) ] ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Attaching the MRP below, AtmFog.gdshader and SkyMaterial.gdshader are at play here for this plugin. [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25160130/MRP.zip)
